question.text: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)
question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the last available daily value of the ICE BofA US High Yield OAS published on the [FRED website](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2) for the final calendar day (typically the final Friday) of the corresponding biweekly period.
question.fine_print:
* If the FRED data is delayed, the value will be taken as soon as published for the relevant date.
* If the market is closed on the scheduled ending date or if no value for that date is published by FRED for two weeks, the most recent available value from an earlier day in the period will be used.
* Only the initially published value for each date will be used (no revisions).
* The value is reported in percentage points.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-30: FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 latest value is **3.44** (the 3.26 posted for Oct 29 was itself up 12 bp from 3.14 on Oct 28). Oct 30 was the widest close in the recent run and is above the Oct 22-23 peak of 3.38-3.40. [FRED txt](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/BAMLH0A0HYM2.txt)
- The question resolves on the value FRED publishes for Friday 2026-11-20. FRED usually posts with a lag of about one business day, and only the first published print counts.
- One discrepancy: Macrotrends showed 3.32 for Oct 29 while FRED showed 3.26, so third-party mirrors can differ from FRED. [macrotrends](https://www.macrotrends.net/3229/us-high-yield-bond-spread)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet; the target date is 14 trading days after the last print. The spread is at 3.44, near the top of the question's 1.745-3.745 range (30 bp below the ceiling).
- Recent daily moves have been large, with several days of 10 bp or more: +18 bp on Oct 30, +12 on Oct 29, -12 on Oct 26 and +13 on Oct 22. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/BAMLH0A0HYM2.txt)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Naked Capitalism, citing the FT, says US CCC yields are above 18% (about 15% at the start of the year). It also reports that CDS on Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle hit their highest levels since 2021, that Oracle trades like a single-B credit, and that the Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Oct 30. Drivers it cites: AI debt issuance (above $600bn in 2026), rising global rates and high energy prices tied to the Middle East conflict. [nakedcapitalism](https://www.nakedcapitalism.com/2026/11/junk-bond-market-starts-to-crack-in-further-sign-ai-end-game-is-nearing.html)
- 2026-11-02: FXStreet says the Nasdaq 100 fell about 3.5% on Oct 30 and gold dropped to about $3,881, and frames the move as a liquidity squeeze. [fxstreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/why-is-gold-falling-alongside-tech-stocks-a-closer-look-at-liquidity-and-the-bond-market-202611020135)
- 2026-10-30: a Reuters report, cited secondhand, says the Nasdaq 100 was expected to lose more than $2T in value in October on doubts about AI spending. [tech-insider](https://tech-insider.org/nasdaq-100-2-trillion-october-wipeout-ai-spending-fears-2026)
- 2026-10-29: Bloomberg reports the gap between the best- and worst-rated European junk bonds is the widest in more than 17 years. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/junk-market-splits-as-european-spreads-hit-widest-since-2009)
- 2026-10-28: the FOMC reportedly held rates at 3.75-4.00% on a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack preferring a hike. The market is reportedly pricing a December hike, and one source puts the FedWatch odds at about 85%. I could not verify this against federalreserve.gov, and sources disagree on what the Fed did before October. [admiralmarkets](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/fomc-october-2026-fed-holds-rates)
- 2026-10-27: Lead-Lag Report says CCC OAS hit 13.56% on Oct 23, the widest in FRED's 3-year daily window and above the April 2025 high of 11.37%. MarketsFN put the overall high-yield spread at 338 bp on Oct 27, but FRED shows 3.18 that day. [leadlag](https://www.leadlagreport.com/junk-bonds-split-in-two-ccc-spreads-are-wider-than-april-2025/), [marketsfn](https://www.marketsfn.com/article/credit-spreads-daily-2026-10-27)
- 2026-10-09: CNBC says junk bonds are "flashing yellow" with spreads at their widest since April. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/09/junk-bonds-are-flashing-yellow-watch-these-warning-signs.html)
- A JunkBondInvestor note argues the CCC widening is concentrated in a handful of idiosyncratic issuers. [junkbondinvestor](https://www.junkbondinvestor.com/p/credit-weekly-the-ccc-myth)

## 4. Base rates and recent trend
- The trend is clearly upward. Selected FRED closes:

| Sep 21 (low) | 2.66 |
| Oct 1 | 3.24 |

| Oct 30 | 3.44 |

  That is roughly +78 bp in about six weeks. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/BAMLH0A0HYM2.txt)
- Two-week windows recently: Oct 9 to Oct 23 moved +27 bp; Sep 25 to Oct 9 moved +18 bp; Oct 16 to Oct 30 moved +13 bp.
- The provided empirical baseline (14-trading-day changes since 2005, recent years double-weighted, applied to 3.44):

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OAS | 3.05 | 3.16 | 3.30 | 3.40 | 3.53 | 3.70 | 3.83 |

  The baseline does not account for the current high-volatility regime. Recent daily moves of 10-18 bp suggest the spread of outcomes may be wider than the historical average.
- The 3.745 ceiling sits around the baseline's p90-p95. For context, in the April 2025 tariff shock the spread peaked at about 4.5% before falling back fast; that is from memory, not checked in this session.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the high-yield OAS itself.
- Related Kalshi Treasury markets (Nov 2026) put about a 49% chance on the 2-year yield touching 4.72% and about a 42% chance on the 30-year reaching 5.40%. That points to high rate levels and rate volatility, not a forecast for spreads.
- Polymarket shows the 10-year has already reached 5.2% this year, with about a 9% chance of 5.5% before 2027.
- I found no sell-side forecast for the high-yield OAS in mid-November.

## 6. Upcoming events before Nov 20
- 2026-11-03: US midterm elections (date from the electoral calendar, not sourced in this session).
- 2026-11-06: October jobs report, 8:30 ET. [thriveinmarkets](https://thriveinmarkets.com/calendar/dates/nfp-2026/)
- Around Nov 10-13: October CPI. I could not confirm the exact date.
- 2026-11-17: Nvidia FQ3 results after the close. This is a key AI-sentiment catalyst given that the stress is concentrated in AI-linked credit. [NVIDIA IR](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Sets-Conference-Call-for-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx)
- Ongoing risks: Fed hike pricing for the Dec 8-9 FOMC, heavy AI and hyperscaler debt issuance, and energy prices tied to the Middle East.
- Calendar note: Nov 11 (Veterans Day) is a bond-market holiday, so there are probably no FRED prints that day. Nov 20 is a normal trading day.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The forecast window closes Nov 9, and the outcome will be known around Nov 20-23, 2026. The target is the FRED print for Friday Nov 20, which is about 14 trading days after the last observation.

(b) The latest known value is 3.44 on 2026-10-30 (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2).

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be 3.44.

(d) If the six-week trend of roughly +13 bp per week continued for three more weeks, the outcome would be about 3.80. The trend has been choppy, with sharp reversals such as -21 bp from Oct 1 to Oct 6 and -20 bp from Oct 23 to Oct 28.

(e) Historically, the 14-day changes give a range of about 3.05 to 3.83 (p5 to p95) around 3.44. Current daily volatility is about 10 bp, which implies a standard deviation of about 35-40 bp over this horizon. That is wider than the historical baseline, and widening shocks have fat right tails.

(f) I found no direct market or expert forecast for the spread. The surrounding signals point to continued stress:
- CCC yields above 18%.
- Hyperscaler CDS at multi-year highs.
- The Fed hike being priced for December.
- Treasury yields high and volatile.

There is also some mean reversion in spreads after sharp jumps, as shown by the April 2025 spike and quick retracement.

(g) Scenarios:
- **Low outcome:** A soft CPI, strong Nvidia results on Nov 17 and dovish Fed communication trigger a relief rally. Spreads fall back to around 2.9-3.0.
- **High outcome:** A disorderly sell-off in AI credit (Oracle or hyperscaler issuance failing), the Fed hike confirmed, and an energy shock push spreads to 4.3-4.8, comparable to April 2025.

- **High:** The AI-capex credit scare could spread, with a hyperscaler or Oracle downgrade, a failed deal or fund redemptions, combined with a hawkish shock. The spread would gap toward the April 2025 peak of about 4.5%.
